newsitem.title: CHINA: China says eager to join WTO, but has patience.
newsitem.headline: China says eager to join WTO, but has patience.

text.p: Chinese Premier Li Peng said on Friday delays in China's accession to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) were abnormal but Beijing very much wanted to join and had sufficient patience to wait for membership.
"I think it is abnormal that China cannot join the WTO for such a long time," Li told a news conference after the close of the annual session of the National People's Congress, or parliament.
However, the premier said he was optimistic despite the delays.
"China is a major trading country and would very much like to join this organisation," Li said.

Beijing's bid to join the WTO has been held up partly because it wants to join on the easier terms accorded a developing country. Some Western nations, including the United States, insist China's economy is too big for such treatment.
"China is a developing country... China will not accept developed country standards forced on it," Li stressed.
"Chinese have sufficient patience," Li said. "I hope the countries concerned will be wise and resolve this problem as early as possible.
"Not only does the WTO need China, but China also needs the WTO," he said.

China's bid for accession to the WTO had made major progress in talks in Geneva this month but many obstacles remained ahead, the China Daily quoted the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation as saying in a statement.

During talks in Geneva March 4-6, foreign trade assistant minister Long Yongtu pledged that China would make its foreign trade rights freely available for domestic and foreign investors within three years, the newspaper said.
But more thorny issues remained to be resolved.
"We should realise that in upcoming talks, a number of thorny issues concerning accession protocol and market access remain unsolved," the ministry said.
"We hope the negotiations will progress. Chances are the talks will bear fruit," it said.
Intensive talks are anticipated on two-way market access, particularly service trade market access, the ministry said.

Progress in the talks would depend on whether parties involved can strike a final agreement on the basis of an overall balance of rights and obligations, while bearing in mind the current stage of economic development in China, it said.
"We are willing to continue our talks with all contracting parties," the ministry said.
"A growing number of WTO members have the goodwill to accelerate the process of China's accession into the WTO," the ministry said.
"It is a consensus of all WTO members that China's entry is conducive to strengthening the multinational trade region," it said.
